rows.query: What do you have to tell me before you give me a price?
rows.why: The mandatory disclosure must be stated before any plan price is discussed.

results.title: Mandatory disclosures
results.content: At the start of every call the agent must state that the call is recorded for quality and compliance purposes. Before discussing any plan price, the agent must state that final coverage and premiums are subject to medical underwriting and depend on verified medical history. If the customer does not consent to recording, the agent must end the automated conversation and offer a callback from a human advisor.

rows.query: Can you guarantee that my diabetes will be covered?
rows.why: Agents may never guarantee coverage of a pre-existing condition; the FAQ explains coverage depends on medical underwriting.

results.title: Are pre-existing conditions covered?
results.content: Pre-existing conditions must be declared on the application. Depending on medical underwriting, a condition may be covered in full, covered with a specific exclusion, or covered with an additional premium. An advisor cannot confirm the outcome during a call.

results.title: Prohibited statements
results.content: Agents must never guarantee approval or coverage of a pre-existing condition, quote a final premium, give medical advice or diagnoses, disparage another insurer, or pressure the customer to decide during the call.

results.title: Family Shield - Getting a family quote
results.content: To prepare a family quote, the advisor needs the age of every family member, the state of residence, tobacco use for each adult, and any pre-existing condition for each person. A family quote is an estimate only and does not guarantee coverage for pre-existing conditions.

rows.query: I want to speak to a real person.

results.title: Human escalation
results.content: Transfer the caller to a licensed human advisor when the caller asks for a person, raises a complaint, asks a detailed medical or legal question, or disputes a claim on an existing policy. Human advisors are available Monday to Friday 8 AM to 8 PM Central Time and Saturday 9 AM to 2 PM Central Time. Outside these hours, schedule a callback within 1 business day.

results.title: Eligibility rules
results.content: Essential Care is available to applicants aged 18 to 64. Family Shield is available to a policyholder aged 18 to 64 together with eligible dependents. Senior Secure is available to applicants aged 55 to 75. Applicants must live in a state where plans are offered: Texas, Florida, Georgia, Arizona, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Michigan, Tennessee, Colorado, or Virginia.

results.title: Preliminary lead qualification
results.content: A lead must be referred to a senior health advisor when the caller reports cancer treatment in the last 5 years, kidney dialysis, an organ transplant, or a current hospital admission. A lead is not eligible for a quote when the caller lives outside the offered states or no plan matches the caller's age. Offer to notify the caller when plans become available in their state. Agents provide a preliminary outcome only.

rows.query: What information do you need from me to qualify?
rows.why: The qualification questions record lists the details collected and their order.

results.title: Preliminary lead qualification
results.content: Agents provide a preliminary outcome only. Final eligibility is decided by medical underwriting after a complete application.

results.title: Qualification questions
results.content: Ask one question at a time, in this order: the caller's age, state of residence, how many people need coverage and their ages, tobacco use, any current medical conditions, current insurance, the best time for a callback, and consent to be contacted. If an answer conflicts with an earlier answer, politely read back both answers and ask the caller which one is correct. Never guess a missing detail.

results.title: Objection: I do not want to share medical information on the phone
results.content: Explain that health details are needed only so medical underwriting can give an accurate premium. The caller may skip the question and complete it later through the secure application or with a licensed advisor.

rows.query: I had a kidney transplant last year, can I still apply?
rows.why: An organ transplant requires referral to a senior health advisor under the preliminary qualification rules.

results.title: Preliminary lead qualification
results.content: A lead is preliminarily qualified when the caller's age is within the range of at least one plan, the caller lives in a state where plans are offered, and the caller consents to be contacted. A lead must be referred to a senior health advisor when the caller reports cancer treatment in the last 5 years, kidney dialysis, an organ transplant, or a current hospital admission.

rows.query: How long is the waiting period?
rows.why: The waiting-period FAQ gives 30 days for non-emergency care and 12 months for specific surgeries.

results.title: Is there a waiting period before my coverage starts?
results.content: Yes. There is a 30-day waiting period for non-emergency services from the policy start date. Accidents and emergencies are covered from day one. Planned joint replacement and cataract surgery have a 12-month waiting period.

rows.query: Can I get a refund if I cancel?
rows.why: The cancellation FAQ describes the 30-day free-look full refund.

results.title: Can I cancel my policy?
results.content: Every new policy has a 30-day free-look period. If you cancel within 30 days of the policy start date and have made no claims, you receive a full premium refund.

rows.query: What if I pay my premium late?
rows.why: The missed-payment FAQ describes the 30-day grace period and lapse.

results.title: What happens if I miss a premium payment?
results.content: There is a 30-day grace period after the premium due date. Coverage continues during the grace period. If the premium is not paid by the end of the grace period, the policy lapses.

rows.query: How do I file a claim at a hospital?

results.title: How do I make a claim?
results.content: At in-network providers, claims are cashless: show your member card and the provider bills Darwix Health directly. For out-of-network emergency care, submit a reimbursement claim with itemized bills within 90 days of discharge. Complete claims are processed within 15 business days.

results.title: Objection: Insurance companies never pay claims
results.content: Acknowledge the frustration. Explain that claims at in-network providers are cashless and that complete reimbursement claims are processed within 15 business days. Never guarantee that a specific claim will be approved.
